episode_title: Save the Deal or Hand Back the Keys? Mark Kenney - Think Multifamily

real_qa.q: What caused multifamily deals to fail during the 2022-2025 market downturn despite prior success?
real_qa.r: Interest rates on floating-rate bridge debt went from 4% to 10-11% between 2022 and 2023, while rents stagnated or declined and tenants fell behind on payments. Insurance costs spiked dramatically—Florida saw 200-300% increases, and one South Texas property went from 1.2 to 3.6 million annually. Combined with massive oversupply in multifamily and properties worth far less than their loan balances, operators had to choose between throwing capital at deals to extend runway or handing back keys to lenders, with many finding that even 12-24 month loan modifications proved insufficient.
real_qa.requete: Why did multifamily deals fail 2023 2024 downturn

real_qa.q: What property tax assessment shock did Think Multifamily experience and how did it impact deal feasibility?
real_qa.r: One Think Multifamily property valued around 10 million had its property tax assessment frozen for four years, then the county tried to raise it to 21 million in a single year with no logical support. Lenders often require escrow of the full disputed amount even during appeals, forcing operators to tie up capital on uncertain liabilities. This unpredictability—varying significantly by county—became a critical factor in underwriting and deal viability.
real_qa.requete: Property tax assessment increase 10 million 21 million county

real_qa.q: How did cap rate expansion from 2022 to 2024 make it impossible to sell properties at loan payoff?
real_qa.r: In parts of Florida, cap rates expanded from 4.4% in 2022 to 7.5% by 2024, leaving properties completely underwater relative to their loan balances. Properties that brokers valued at 9-10 million prior to 2022 were receiving offers at 17 million or less by 2023-2024, making it impossible to sell and pay off the loan with any remaining equity or proceeds.

real_qa.q: What percentage of multifamily deals in 2024-2025 could not be sold without a shortfall to the lender?
real_qa.r: Mark stated that a high percentage of deals—not single-digit—could not be sold in 2024-2025 while still paying off the loan balance. He emphasized this was the norm, not the exception, forcing operators to either work with lenders on modifications or strategically default rather than take a loss and still come up short to the lender.
real_qa.requete: Percentage deals 2024 2025 cannot sell pay off loan

real_qa.q: What is the required cash-on-cash return for multifamily deals to attract capital in the current market environment?
real_qa.r: In the current environment with risk-free CDs yielding 5% or higher, investors expect cash-on-cash returns close to that risk-free alternative to justify equity investment. If multifamily deals cannot deliver cash-on-cash yields competitive with liquid risk-free investments, it becomes very difficult to raise capital, even accounting for tax benefits and long-term appreciation.
real_qa.requete: Required cash on cash return multifamily CDs 5 percent

guest.bio_context: Mark Kenney has over 30 years of operating experience in multifamily real estate, including more than 120 multifamily deals totaling 18,000 units and more than 1 billion in closed transactions across 15 states. He exited 20 deals in 2024 alone and started his real estate journey in college with his identical twin brother, initially purchasing small 2-4 unit properties before transitioning to syndications in 2015. He was a CPA who worked for the Big Four and later started an IT consulting company before pivoting to multifamily investments through syndications.

real_quote: When you run out of money, it happens very quickly. Four to eight weeks and your occupancy goes from 97% to the 70s because you can't even turn units.
